items.text:
The  use  of  renewable  energy  has  become  a  global  priority  as countries  strive  to  reduce  their  dependence  on  fossil  fuels. Renewable sources such as solar, wind, and hydroelectric power offer cleaner alternatives that help lower carbon emissions and combat  climate  change.  However,  the  transition  to  renewable energy  is  not  without  challenges.  The  initial  cost  of setting up infrastructure remains high,  and  energy  production  can  be inconsistent due to weather conditions. Despite these drawbacks,  technological  innovations  are  making  renewable energy more efficient and affordable.
Governments are  also  encouraging  the shift through subsidies, tax incentives, and investment in research. These measures not only help reduce environmental damage but also create employment  opportunities  in  new  sectors.  Public  awareness about  sustainability  has  further  accelerated  the  demand  for cleaner  energy  options.  The  future  of  global  energy  lies  in  a balanced  approach-using  renewable  sources  while  continuing to  improve  storage  technologies  and  grid  efficiency.  If  nations maintain this momentum, renewable energy could soon replace conventional sources as the dominant form of power.
SSC CGL 14/09/2025 (Shift 3)

items.text: In  the  contemporary  world, silence has become an anomaly-an absence that many mistake for emptiness rather than presence. Yet,  silence  is not the negation of sound but its most profound counterpoint.  It  is  within  silence  that  reflection  finds  its  voice, that thoughts distill into clarity, and that creativity germinates. In an age dominated by incessant notifications, ceaseless commentary, and performative expression, the ability to be silent is increasingly radical. Philosophers from Lao Tzu to Wittgenstein  have  observed  that  language,  though  powerful, often fractures experience into fragments that silence alone can reconcile.  True  understanding,  therefore,  may  not  always  lie  in articulation  but  in  the  spaces  between  words-the  pauses  that lend  speech  its  meaning.  Moreover,  silence  carries  moral  and emotional  weight.  It  can  soothe  or  wound, liberate or oppress. The silence of complicity sustains injustice, while the silence of contemplation heals. Moreover,  silence  carries  moral  and emotional  weight.  It  can  soothe  or  wound, liberate or oppress. The silence of complicity sustains injustice, while the silence of contemplation heals. In relationships, silence can communicate intimacy or alienation, depending on intent and context. Thus, to master  silence  is  not  to  abstain  from  speech  but  to  discern when words enhance truth and when they obscure it. In learning to listen-to others, to nature, to ourselves-we recover a dimension  of  awareness  long  buried  beneath  the  noise  of modern life. Silence, then, is not absence but essence: the quiet pulse  beneath  the  surface  of  existence  that  restores  depth  to being.

Yet,  silence  is not the negation of sound but its most profound counterpoint.  It  is  within  silence  that  reflection  finds  its  voice, that thoughts distill into clarity, and that creativity germinates.
